resources.string: The sensor service lists no sensor: the sensors HAL (android.hardware.sensors) is not running or fails to start. Check logcat for sensorservice and the vendor sensor daemon.
SensorManager is unavailable: system_server did not start sensorservice.
Accelerometer, proximity and light sensor present

A phone normally has these. Without proximity the screen stays on against the ear during calls; without the light sensor auto-brightness does nothing. Check that the driver probes (dmesg) and that the sensors HAL lists it (on Qualcomm: the SSC sensor registry or the sensors configuration in vendor).
The ROM declares android.hardware.sensor.* features for sensors the HAL does not list, so apps expect them. Remove the permission XML from PRODUCT_COPY_FILES or fix the HAL.
The HAL lists these sensors but the device tree does not copy the feature XMLs (frameworks/native/data/etc/android.hardware.sensor.*.xml): some apps and app stores then hide functions.
Angle between the two gravity vectors: %1$s°

The fused gravity points elsewhere than the raw accelerometer: the fusion uses a different orientation matrix (axis remap) than the driver, so rotation and compass are wrong. Check the axis configuration of the sensors HAL.
Body sensors need the BODY_SENSORS permission, which this app does not request.
The HAL lists the sensor but refuses to activate it: activate()/batch() fails in the sensors HAL. Look for sensorservice errors in logcat.

The sensor is listed and activated but delivers nothing: the driver or firmware is not streaming (on Qualcomm: the SSC on the ADSP, the sensors daemon or a missing registry entry). Fusion sensors built on it stay silent too.
Normal for an on-change sensor when nothing changes. It should still report its current value right after activation: if the guided test stays silent too, the driver is not reporting.
%1$d events contain NaN or infinity: the HAL passes uninitialised values or divides by zero.
Timestamps go backwards %1$d times: broken HAL timestamps break fusion and rate calculations.
Events arrive %1$s ms after their timestamp: the timestamps are not in the elapsedRealtimeNanos clock (a CTS requirement), or the HAL batches although no batching was requested.
Delivers %1$s Hz although %2$s Hz was requested within the declared minDelay: the HAL cannot reach the rate it advertises (wrong minDelay or output data rate in the driver).
All %1$d samples are identical: the driver returns a cached value instead of reading the sensor.
Events carry only %1$d values, fewer than this sensor type requires.
Every value is exactly 0: the sensor is not powered or not configured (regulator, wrong I2C address, or the HAL sends empty events).
|a| ≈ 1: the HAL reports in g instead of m/s² (the ×9.81 conversion is missing).
The values change a lot: the phone moved during the test. Repeat with the phone lying still.
|a| is off by a factor of two from 9.81 m/s²: the driver converts with the wrong full-scale range.
|a| should be 9.81 ± 1.5 m/s² at rest: wrong scale factor or a large uncalibrated offset.
The fusion output is all zeros: the fusion has no input (its accelerometer or gyroscope does not stream).
Gravity should be 9.81 m/s²: the fusion is fed by a mis-scaled accelerometer.
Linear acceleration at rest is ≈ 9.81 m/s²: gravity is not removed, the fusion is broken.
Linear acceleration should be ≈ 0 at rest: wrong gravity estimate or accelerometer offset.
Exact zeros at rest. Some ICM/MPU gyroscopes do this when still; the guided rotation test decides whether it works.
The gyroscope reads a rotation while the phone is still: bias not calibrated or wrong scale.
The uncalibrated output includes the bias; a large value at rest means a large offset.
The field is about ten times the Earth\'s: probably milligauss or raw counts instead of µT (scale in the HAL).
The Earth\'s field is 20–70 µT: the magnetometer needs calibration (figure-eight motion), a magnet is nearby, or the scale is wrong.
Uncalibrated field minus the bias estimate is outside 20–70 µT; normal before the first calibration.
x²+y²+z² exceeds 1: the output is not a unit quaternion, the fusion is broken.
The quaternion norm is not 1: the HAL fills the w component wrongly.
Air pressure is 300–1100 hPa: wrong unit (Pa or kPa) or an uncalibrated sensor.
Negative illuminance: the driver converts the raw counts wrongly.
Over 200,000 lx, brighter than direct sunlight: wrong conversion factor.
Values outside 0 to the maximum range: the HAL reports raw ADC counts instead of centimetres, while apps compare with the maximum range to decide near or far.
Reports several distances, not only near and far (allowed).
Relative humidity outside 0 to 100: wrong conversion.
Negative value: conversion error in the driver.
Do what each test asks: the result is saved as soon as the sensor reacts.
Reported as not reacting by the tester
Cover the top of the phone, near the earpiece, with your hand, then uncover it. Repeat twice.
No events at all: the proximity driver does not report, so the screen will not turn off during calls.
Always near: wrong threshold or calibration (proximity calibration in persist, or a dirty or covered window). The screen would stay off during calls.
Never near: threshold too high, IR LED not powered or the reading is not converted.
Cover the sensor with a finger, then point the phone at a lamp or a window.
No events: the light sensor driver does not report, so auto-brightness cannot work.
The value barely changes: wrong gain or integration time, wrong conversion, or the sensor sits behind an opaque part of the panel.
Rotate the phone quickly left and right a few times.
No events: the gyroscope does not stream.
Only zeros while rotating: the gyroscope is not enabled in the driver or its FIFO is never read.
Peak of only %1$s rad/s while rotating: wrong full-scale range in the driver.
Lay the phone face up on a table, then turn it face down.
Z is negative: if the screen faces up, the Z axis is inverted.
Z is negative with the screen facing up: the accelerometer orientation matrix (sensors HAL or device tree) inverts Z. Screen rotation and games are affected.
Z never reached ±9.8 m/s² as asked: swapped axes or wrong scale. Check the orientation matrix of the driver.
Heading from the rotation vector, or from accelerometer and magnetometer.
If the heading is wrong, move the phone in a figure eight a few times, away from metal and magnets.
Does the red needle point north? Compare with a map or a real compass.
%1$d sensors. Tap one to see its values.
Updates only when the value changes.
Below half of the declared maximum (%1$s Hz).
One-shot sensor: arm it, then do what triggers it (for significant motion, walk a few steps).
